title: a lineage
hook: a boy at a teacher's door is asked his family line, and he doesn't know it
tomorrow: how can Krishna say he taught the sun?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a lineage was a list: the Brihadaranyaka's line of teachers, name by name, ending with a bow to Brahman. Today, a boy whose name has no list behind it.
screen: `THE LINE OF TEACHERS.` · `TODAY: NO LIST AT ALL.`

segments.voice: Every application asks for it somewhere: name, date of birth, parents' names. Now a boy is standing at a teacher's door with one question to answer, and he doesn't know the answer. His name is Satyakama. He's come to ask the teacher, Gautama, to take him as a student. And the teacher asks what anyone would ask: what's your gotra, your family line? A lie would be easy. Nobody would check.
screen: `NAME, BIRTH, PARENTS.` → `A BOY AT THE TEACHER'S DOOR.` → `WHAT'S YOUR FAMILY LINE?`

segments.voice: Back home, he'd already asked his mother, Jabala. In the Chandogya Upanishad she answers plainly: I don't know your line, son. I was young, working as a servant in many houses, when I had you. I am Jabala; you are Satyakama. Call yourself Satyakama Jabala. So at the door, he says exactly that, word for word. He doesn't polish it. And Gautama says: no one who wasn't a true brahmin could speak like this. Bring the fuel; I'll take you as a student. You have not left the truth. Then the teacher sends him off with a herd of thin, weak cows, and Satyakama says he won't come back until the herd has grown. Out with the cows, the teaching comes to him from strange teachers: a bull, the fire, a swan, a diving bird. When he finally walks home, his teacher looks at him and says: you shine like one who knows Brahman. So where did this lineage start? Not with a list of names. It started with a sentence that cost something to say. In this story, the truth was the line.
screen: `I DON'T KNOW YOUR LINE, SON.` · `HE SAYS IT WORD FOR WORD.` · `YOU HAVE NOT LEFT THE TRUTH.` · `THE TRUTH WAS THE LINE.`

segments.voice: Look at one thing near you that came to you from someone: a photo, a ring, a cup, a book. Don't weigh what it's worth. Let what you know of its story, and what you don't, sit there with you while you breathe.
A lineage: in Satyakama's story, a line of teaching that begins with a boy telling the truth about not knowing his own.
Your line: a lineage. Sometimes it starts with one honest sentence at a door. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Satyakama's story is retold in Hindu homes and classes as a story about truthfulness; some families still ask a person's gotra at weddings and rites, and the story is often brought up beside that custom.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 4.4.1–4.4.5 (Satyakama asks his mother Jabala his gotra; she does not know: in youth, going about much as a servant, she had him; she is Jabala, he is Satyakama; he says the same to Haridrumata Gautama, who says none but a brahmin could speak so, bring the fuel, I will initiate you, you have not gone from the truth; he is given lean, weak cows and will not return until they have multiplied)
Chandogya Upanishad 4.5–4.9 (the bull, the fire, a swan and a diving bird teach him; his teacher: you shine like one who knows Brahman)

notes: Story shape: the hook drops into the scene at the door; the teach answers the cliffhanger.

Satyakama was likely taught in year two's Chandogya block; this day takes the angle of a lineage that begins with an honest answer. He reappears as Upakosala's teacher on 1789, where he says to his own student the line once said to him ('you shine like one who knows Brahman'); that link is held for 1789.

The text gives the herd as four hundred cows and the goal as a thousand; the script says 'a herd of thin, weak cows' and 'until the herd has grown' to avoid the numbers. The mother's words (4.4.2) are rendered gently ('working as a servant in many houses'); confirm tone. A parent note: the story touches a child not knowing his father; handled in one plain line.
Gautama's 'no one who wasn't a true brahmin could speak like this' is reported as the teacher's words, not endorsed as a rule about birth; confirm framing.
howItsDone mentions gotra being asked at weddings and rites; confirm.
